focus: Current-reference tonight with hypothetical vomiting
reason: A possible event tonight belongs to the local submission date without proving occurrence.

focus: Current-reference tonight with an actual episode
reason: A completed episode tonight uses the same current-day anchor as a hypothetical claim, with different assertion and count.

focus: Current-reference this evening with hypothetical nausea
reason: This evening has a resolvable local date even though the symptom is only a possibility.

focus: Current-reference this evening with actual nausea
reason: An actual evening symptom has a date but no supported clock time or numeric severity.

focus: Today across a UTC-to-Pacific date boundary
reason: The UTC timestamp is December 5 while the patient-local date is December 4; the explicit clock is retained.

focus: Yesterday across a UTC-to-Tokyo date boundary
reason: Local submission is December 7, so yesterday is December 6; a whole-day total is not a current-day snapshot.

focus: Explicit historical date with a partial-day window
reason: The afternoon interval supplies a date and window count but neither an exact clock nor a whole-day total.

focus: Today with an explicit clock and one episode
reason: A precise event time identifies an episode without implying an all-day cumulative count.

focus: Meal-relative window with an explicitly unknown day
reason: Submission context cannot supply a missing meal date, and a meal is not an exact clock.

focus: Known current-day window with unknown episode count
reason: Several confirms occurrence without supplying an exact integer; the ride supplies only a window.

focus: Explicit absence of both target symptoms
reason: Explicit absence supports zero vomiting episodes, while nausea has no episode-count field.

focus: One count over an explicit multi-day range
reason: The combined count must stay unallocated because the schema cannot represent a date range as one event date.

focus: Eligible severity disagreement with agreeing positive counts
reason: The text score remains 3 before reconciliation; only severity is unresolved because count and presence agree.

focus: Current-only score on the otherwise supported scale
reason: A current rating must not be reinterpreted as the worst rating so far today.

focus: Unsupported text scale with an independently valid questionnaire rating
reason: The form can supply severity 2 while the rejected 6-of-10 text score remains a source diagnostic, without conversion.

focus: Supported scale with unspecified score context
reason: A date and scale do not establish whether the rating describes current severity or the worst so far today.

focus: Two target symptoms on different relative dates
reason: Separate clauses carry their own dates; the report-level submission date must not collapse them.

focus: Different positive daily counts from text and questionnaire
reason: Text count 4 survives extraction, then count becomes unknown while agreed presence stays present.

focus: Text absence versus positive questionnaire count
reason: Zero in the source must be preserved before reconciliation marks both presence and number as conflicting.

focus: Unrelated text with no target symptom
reason: A successful empty extraction must not invent symptom absence, counts, dates, or observations.
